test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 15 Nov 2021 Shift 2
subject: general
question:
**Given here are four sentences. The first sentence is in correct order, while the rest of the sentences are jumbled. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. Residents in Ryde, Isle of Wight have been living with a stench from rotting seaweed, which smells like raw sewage.

B. Diggers have been brought in to scoop about 300 tonnes of the washed-up seaweed off the beach.

C. The warm weather has made the odour from the seaweed so pungent it is making people feel sick.

D. It will be taken to agricultural fields on the west of the island and used as fertilizer.
solution:
The correct answer is "ACBD"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage. 
 
• Statement A is the opening sentence of the passage which explains that **The odour of rotting seaweed, which smells like raw sewage, has been a source of discomfort for residents of Ryde, Isle of Wight.**
 
• Statement C is the second sentence of the passage which explains that **People are feeling queasy because of how strong the smell of the seaweed has become due to the warm weather.**
 
• Statement B is the third sentence of the passage which explains **To remove around 300 tonnes of the beach-washed seaweed, diggers have been sent in.**
 
• Statement D is the last sentence of the passage which shows that **It will be transported to the island's western agricultural lands where it will be used as fertiliser.**

Hence, the correct sequence is A, C, B, D

The correct answer is option 1.

The correct passage is:* **A**. Residents in Ryde, Isle of Wight have been living with a stench from rotting seaweed, which smells like raw sewage. **C**. The warm weather has made the odour from the seaweed so pungent it is making people feel sick. **B**. Diggers have been brought in to scoop about 300 tonnes of the washed-up seaweed off the beach. **D**. It will be taken to agricultural fields on the west of the island and used as fertilizer. *
